46	pair, with `auth_mode` through `credsFor`. Two ways to read a catalog:
47	
48	- **A Nexus member** (a discovered member of a `provider: nexus` group, or a
49	  `parent:` entry of one, DEVDESK-579) is read on its own path,
50	  `/v2/<repo_prefix>/_catalog`. Nexus (3.98.1-01 Community, measured on the bench
51	  on 2026-11-17) answers with names that do not carry the
52	  prefix; DevDesk rebuilds `<repo_prefix>/<name>`. The pull account gets 200
53	  and the full list on `_catalog`, like admin (same version, bench, 2026-11-17;
54	  hypothesis H2 confirmed). Not measured: an account restricted to one
55	  repository, the company instance. An empty catalog is "no
56	  result"; a 404, 401, 403 or 405 is refused. One walk per member.
57	- **Any other entry** walks the root catalog of its host (`/v2/_catalog`), keeps
58	  the names under `<repo_prefix>/` and matches the typed text on the part after
59	  it. A catalog with no name under the prefix is refused, not "no result".
60	  Entries that share an API URL and an identity share one walk per search
61	  (DEVDESK-311, `network.md`); an entry with other credentials, another port or
62	  another subdomain is walked on its own.
63	
64	**A discovered group is searched as one unit.** The members the detector found
65	with no address of their own (same URL and `repo_prefix` as the group) are merged
66	into one search unit, the group, labelled `<alias> (group)`. Nexus reads the
67	catalog through the group without saying which member holds a name, so rows carry
68	no member. The picker's selection does not narrow this: a single ticked bare
69	member searches the whole group, and an unticked member's name can appear. A
70	group that was never discovered (a pull account) is searched as itself. See
71	`network.md`, "Image search and Nexus members".
72	
73	Three things follow, each with a test:
74	
75	- **The prefix is applied once**, in `submitSearch`. It is then already part of
76	  `MultiRegistryTag.Repo`, so `multiImageName` and `registryAPIURL` know nothing
77	  about it — teaching both would be two places free to drift.
78	- **A group may not declare one**, and `LoadContext` refuses it: a group is
79	  reachable only through its own connector, and the same trick applied to a group
80	  answers 404. `RegistryForm` therefore does not offer the field on a group.
81	- **A URL no longer identifies an entry.** Several entries share one host now, so
82	  `entryFor` resolves by entry key, `resultFilter` holds a key, every
83	  `MultiRegistryTag` carries one, and `memberKey` takes the prefix as a third
84	  segment — a member's URL is its *group's*. `registryRef(url, prefix)` is the one
85	  place an entry becomes something a user reads, and it is the head of the pull
86	  reference exactly.
87	
88	`NexusDetector` synthesises nothing any more. A group written as a path prefix
89	serves its members the same way, so it emits `(host, memberName)` — consistent by
90	construction. Reached through a connector of its own it emits the group's URL and
91	**no** prefix, because which connector a member answers on is precisely what it
92	cannot read: an empty prefix against a bare host is wrong and visibly so, where
93	the synthesised path was wrong and plausible.
94	
95	**`auth_mode` is read before any credential lookup**, on both paths that talk to
96	a registry: `detectRegistryGroupCmd` and the browser's `credsFor`. `anonymous`
97	sends nothing, not even a configured username. This is what `auth_enabled` never
98	did (D12): `docker login` is keyed on host, so one login against a Nexus
99	instance used to authenticate every repository it serves.
100	
101	That same host-keying is why a **member cannot declare `credentials` of its
102	own** — it shares its group's single credential entry, so a password of its own
103	has nowhere to go — and why `inherit` on an entry with no group is refused.
104	Both are load-time errors.
105	
106	An entry whose URL carries a path (a Nexus `/repository/<name>` connector,
107	`http://127.0.0.1:30481/repository/docker-hosted`) finds that login too
108	(DEVDESK-635): `docker.GetStoredCreds` and `docker.RegistryLoginState` share
109	`credentialPhases`, which looks under the exact address first, then under the
110	entry's `host[:port]` **as written** (`hostKey`, with its `https://` and
111	`http://` variants and the credential helpers asked for that key). The port is
112	never added, dropped or widened: `nexus.example` and `nexus.example:443` are two
113	keys, and a login stored for `127.0.0.1` is not found for an entry on port
114	30481. The exact key wins over the host's. `auth_mode: anonymous` still sends
115	nothing, whatever the lookup could find; `credsFor` reads it first.
116	
117	**The registry host's login never goes to another management host (DEVDESK-629,
118	M1).** `discoveryCreds` (`internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go`) looks at the
119	host of `management_url`: when it is not the registry URL's `host[:port]` (compared
120	case-insensitively, a scheme-less URL read as https), only a login stored for the
121	management host is sent there, and nothing found means anonymous; the registry
122	host's login, which the host key above now finds for a URL with a path, is never
123	used for it. A username or password stated by the user still outranks any stored
124	one. Same host: unchanged.
125	
126	**Known risk, left as is (DEVDESK-629, decided by the user).** A login stored for
127	`h` or `https://h` also serves an entry whose URL is `http://h/path`, so the
128	Basic header goes in clear over http. That was already true for a URL without a
129	path; the host key extends it to a URL with one. A separate story may treat "no
130	Basic over http outside loopback".
131	
132	`internal/config/registries.go` normalizes the list at load and is the only
133	place that decides a slug. Two rules hold it together:
134	
135	- A slug **DevDesk derives** (from the alias, else the URL host) is made unique
136	  by stepping aside — `prod`, `prod-2`. A slug **the file declares** is never
137	  rewritten, because it is a link target; a duplicate, or a `parent` naming no
138	  configured group, makes `LoadContext` fail rather than load a config the
139	  application cannot honour.
140	- An entry from before `kind` existed that carries a `management_url`, **or**
141	  whose URL contains `/repository/`, migrates to `kind: group`,
142	  `provider: nexus` — those were the two things `NexusDetector.CanHandle` used
143	  to accept. A kind the file states is never second-guessed.
144	
145	`provider` is what picks the detector in `internal/registrymgr`: `DetectGroup`
146	matches `Detector.Provider()` against the declared value and falls back to
147	`GenericDetector`, which discovers nothing. A registry is probed because it was
148	declared as something, never because its URL looked like it — so registration
149	order decides nothing, and a plain registry costs no HTTP call. The provider
150	names are stated in both packages on purpose; `TestTheProviderVocabularyMatchesTheConfig`
151	keeps them in step.
152	
153	`RegistryForm` is what keeps the file loadable: it refuses a duplicate or
154	badly-formed slug instead of correcting it, and drops the group-only fields when
155	the kind is not a group.
156

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Bordures étaient soustraites deux fois, ce qui tronquait la dernière colonne.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

# Brief — Registre Docker Hub par défaut dans un nouveau contexte

> Statut : idée cadrée avec l'utilisateur ; pas de stories ni de backlog à ce stade.

## Vision en une phrase

Quand DevDesk crée un nouveau contexte, il y écrit d'emblée le registre Docker Hub (`docker.io`), pour que la
recherche et le pull d'images fonctionnent dès le premier lancement, sans configuration préalable.

## Problème

Aujourd'hui l'utilisateur doit configurer lui-même un registre avant de pouvoir puller ou chercher une
image : la liste de registres d'un contexte neuf est vide, et le premier lancement n'est pas bon.
Hypothèse : à vérifier (ce que l'utilisateur voit exactement avec une liste vide, dans `:oci` et dans la
recherche d'images ; la config d'un contexte neuf vient de `Default()`, voir « À vérifier »).

## Utilisateur

Le mainteneur, utilisateur principal de DevDesk, et tout nouvel utilisateur qui crée un contexte
(`:context new`, `dk setup` ou premier lancement).

## Périmètre MVP

- À la création d'un **nouveau** contexte, la config contient une entrée Docker Hub : `url: docker.io`,
  `auth_mode: anonymous`, dans la liste plate `RegistryConfig.Registries` (voir
  `docs/architecture/registries.md`).
- L'entrée est écrite dans le fichier du contexte comme n'importe quelle autre : modifiable et supprimable
  par l'utilisateur (via `RegistryForm`, `:cfg` ou à la main).
- Docker Hub est déjà reconnu par le code (`oci.IsDockerHub` : `docker.io` et `registry-1.docker.io`).
  Les valeurs exactes de l'entrée (slug, alias, `provider`, `kind`) sont à fixer à la conception.

## Non-objectifs

- Aucun ajout rétroactif : un contexte existant n'est jamais modifié.
- Pas de registre « intégré » ou non supprimable.
- Pas d'autres registres publics dans le MVP (ghcr.io, quay.io, registry.k8s.io, mcr.microsoft.com…).
- Pas d'écran de suggestions au premier lancement (variante C, écartée).

## Décisions prises (avec l'utilisateur)

1. MVP = Docker Hub seul (variante A).
2. Uniquement pour les nouveaux contextes, jamais pour les existants.
3. Entrée ordinaire de la config du contexte, pas un registre spécial.
